title: Breath — Invisible Force, Visible Consequence (archive draft)

events.label: HUMAN / inhale: a young man draws on a cigarette as the lighter is held to it; the draw is breath, its trace (the lit tip, a faint haze at the end) barely visible in daylight. Source voices are NOT his breath (his mouth is closed on the cigarette) -> source audio muted, recorded here (Ask Me, Don't Tell Me, 1961)

HUMAN / exhale shaped as song: singer in close-up, sync song with accompaniment; the audible breaks in the voice near 4.0 s and 8.9 s of the source are his intakes of breath (spectrogram gaps + mouth closing), cut just after the second (Under Western Stars, Republic feature; index year blank)

BRIDGE that exists in the source: the same singer, full figure on stage, while film of a rolling dust storm is projected behind him; voice and wind are joined by that film, not by this edit (Under Western Stars, source t=33.2)
ENVIRONMENTAL wind: a sail cart driven across sand; the cause is unseen, the bellied sail is the trace. Source narration muted (recorded) (The American Road, 1953)
MECHANICAL: the machine is shown first, then the burst of steam/smoke it releases (Master Hands, silent loop)
MECHANICAL: a jet of steam from plant machinery expands and thins; silent print (Steel Mill, 1937 — same shot also appears in The River, 1937, with score)
MECHANICAL: stack steam billowing; source score muted (recorded) (Valley Town, 1940)
RELEASE / stillness: valley mist lying almost unmoved; no source audio; the absence of motion after wind and steam (Valley Fog, 2006)
